A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices describing the same FSM research. The shared taxonomy and experiments can be matched despite v2's substantial extension into reasoning control.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, annotated reasoning trajectories, state frequencies, transition probabilities and FSM lengths on AIME25 and GPQA Diamond.

after.justification: v2 reports original steering experiments across four benchmarks, supplemented by transfer, sensitivity, diversity, intervention-effectiveness and failure analyses.

M1.justification: The six-state taxonomy is retained, but v2 adds an inference-control system absent from v1: outcome-conditioned transition rewards, learned state classifiers, contrastive transition vectors, Q-value planning, confidence-based intervention gating and orthogonal activation steering (Section 3). This substantially changes the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MATH-500 and GSM8K, extending mathematical evaluation beyond AIME25 to a broader math collection and grade-school word problems. Scientific question answering remains covered by GPQA Diamond. Its increased sample count is a protocol change, rather than a new domain.

E2.justification: v1 compares unsteered models and reasoning-effort settings. v2 evaluates Q-Value steering against default inference, Greedy and Weighted steering, plus Positive, Negative, Balanced and Cross-Model prompt guidance (Tables 1 and 5). These are substantial additions to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: GPQA evaluation expands from the first 50 questions to 198, and dual sentence/paragraph analysis gives way to sentence-based control. v2 adds token/intervention metrics, classifier train/test splits, held-out steering-layer selection, and a DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B evaluation. These introduce substantial new evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's descriptive trajectory and granularity comparisons, v2 adds second-order tests of the Markov approximation, cross-model transfer, paired steering examples, diversity/fluency checks, rescue/harm analysis, boundary-detection diagnostics and steering-strength sensitivity (Figure 3; Appendices C, F, H–J).

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 for the main experiments. v2 newly reports five seeds per problem and mean ± standard deviation for the diversity/fluency study (Appendix F), plus correlation significance in Appendix C. These additions are limited to supplementary analyses; main accuracy tables still lack uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive steering and diagnostic results; Table 1 newly reports GPT-L AIME25 accuracy of 56.67% with Q-Value steering versus 43.30% default. Unsteered AIME accuracies match v1 up to rounding, while GPQA scores use the expanded sample. v1's detailed sentence/paragraph FSM-length and state-frequency results are removed.

T1.justification: v2 introduces outcome-conditioned transition matrices, the transition-advantage reward and formal control objectives, with Appendix B deriving Q-value updates through a deterministic-MDP reduction. It also revises the FSM alphabet from generated text spans to an epsilon-only alphabet and restricts accepting states to closure.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims an interpretable framework for describing and comparing reasoning. v2 additionally claims latent-state detectability and effective planning-based inference control, emphasizing accuracy gains and sparse interventions. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion substantially broaden the contribution from analysis to active optimization.

C2.justification: v2 shifts interpretation toward planning, intervention efficiency and model-dependent transfer. It adds substantive limitations concerning correlation versus causation, knowledge gaps, classifier errors, sentence boundaries, taxonomy sensitivity and the need for a correctness signal (Appendix E), alongside hypotheses explaining limited gains in the small distilled model.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability link, encoder/classifier architecture and optimization settings, selected intervention layers, steering strengths and thresholds, and prompt-steering templates. The original sentence-annotation prompt and worked example remain in Appendices K and M; the paragraph-annotation prompt is removed.

R1.justification: v2 repositions the contribution against local behavioral steering, particularly SEAL and the retained Venhoff work, and substantially expands discussion of reasoning-graph topology and cognitive foundations. New references include Minegishi, Matsutani, Xiong, Schoenfeld and Nelson; this exceeds bibliographic updates to retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, results, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around reasoning control. Detailed state descriptions move to Appendix A, limitations become an expanded Appendix E, and the earlier descriptive results/discussion narrative is replaced. Original annotation material is reorganized into Appendices K and M.

P2.justification: v1's frequency plots and sentence/paragraph transition displays are replaced by taxonomy, workflow and intervention-example figures. v2 adds advantage heatmaps and substantially redesigned comparison and diagnostic tables. The page template, typography and running headers also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 turns controllability from a potential application in v1 into an explicitly specified, experimentally evaluated method. Tests of the Markov approximation, intervention harms and side effects substantially strengthen validation, while implementation details improve reproducibility documentation. Some superiority claims overreach the evidence—Table 5 shows prompt guidance outperforming Q-Value steering for QWEN on GSM8K—and main accuracies lack uncertainty estimates. These limitations temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in practical validation and diagnostic support.
